texts.text: הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְשָׁלוֹם וְהַעֲמִידֵנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ לְחַיִּים וּפְרוֹשׂ עָלֵינוּ סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶךָ וְתַקְּנֵנוּ בְּעֵצָה טוֹבָה מִלְּפָנֶיךָ וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ וְהָגֵן בַּעֲדֵנוּ וְהָסֵר מֵעָלֵינוּ אוֹיֵב דֶּבֶר וְחֶרֶב וְרָעָב וְיָגוֹן וְהָסֵר שָׂטָן מִלְּפָנֵינוּ וּמֵאַחֲרֵינוּ וּבְצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ תַּסְתִּירֵנוּ כִּי אֵל שׁוֹמְרֵנוּ וּמַצִּילֵנוּ אָתָּה כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אָתָּה וּשְׁמוֹר צֵאתֵנוּ וּבוֹאֵנוּ לְחַיִּים וּלְשָׁלוֹם מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם. וּפְרוֹשׂ עָלֵינוּ סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶךָ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַפּוֹרֵשׂ סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ וְעַל כָּל־עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלָםִ:

וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּת לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּת לְדֹרֹתָם בְּרִית עוֹלָם: בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹת הִיא לְעֹלָם כִּי־שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה יְהוָה אֶת־הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת־הָאָרֶץ וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ:
תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר בַּכֶּסֶה לְיוֹם חַגֵּנוּ: כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב:
וְעַתָּה יִגְדַּל־נָא כֹּחַ אֲדֹנָי כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ לֵאמֹר: זְכֹר רַחֲמֶיךָ יְיָ וַחֲסָדֶיךָ כִּי מֵעוֹלָם הֵמָּה:

יִתְגַּדַּל וְיִתְקַדַּשׁ שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא בְּעָלְמָא דִּי־בְרָא כִרְעוּתֵהּ וְיַמְלִיךְ מַלְכוּתֵהּ בְּחַיֵּיכוֹן וּבְיוֹמֵיכוֹן וּבְחַיֵּי דְכָל־בֵּית־יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּעֲגָלָא וּבִזְמַן קָרִיב, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן.
יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא.

יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח וְיִתְפָּאַר וְיִתְרֹמַם וְיִתְנַשֵּׂא וְיִתְהַדָּר וְיִתְעַלֶּה וְיִתְהַלָּל שְׁמֵהּ דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְעֵלָּא וּלְעֵלָּא מִן־כָּל־בִּרְכָתָא וְשִׁירָתָא תֻּשְׁבְּחָתָא וְנֶחֱמָתָא דַּאֲמִירָן בְּעָלְמָא, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן:

instructions.position: start of paragraph 2, before cue ושמרו

texts.text: Lead us to rest, O Lord our God, in peace, and let us rise, O our King, to life. Spread over us the tent of Thy peace and improve us through good counsel from before Thee. Help us for the sake of Thy Name, protect us and remove from us foe, pestilence, sword, famine and grief. Remove Satan from in front of us and behind us; and in the shadow of Thy wings shelter us, for Thou art God, our guardian and our deliverer, for Thou art God, a gracious and merciful King. Guard our going out and our return to life and peace from now to eternity. Spread over us the tent of Thy peace. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who spreads the tent of peace over us and over all His people Israel and over Jerusalem.

The Children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath to celebrate the Sabbath throughout their generations as an eternal covenant. Between Me and the Children of Israel it shall be a sign for ever, that in six days the Lord created the heavens and the earth and on the seventh day He ceased from work and rested.
Blow the Shofar on the New Moon when the moon is covered on the day of our festival, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob.
And now let the power of the Lord appear great, as Thou hast said. Remember Thy compassion, O Lord and Thy kindnesses, for they exist since eternity.

Exalted and sanctified be His Great Name in the world which He has created according to His will. May His Kingdom be established in your lifetime and in your days and in the lifetime of the whole House of Israel, speedily and in a short time, and say: Amen!
May His Great Name be praised to eternity and the eternity of eternities!

Blessed and praised and glorified and elevated and exalted and adorned and raised on high and lauded be the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He; high, yea high, above all blessing and song, praise and comfort that have ever been spoken in the world, and say Amen!

decisions.evidence: s24 band1: in Rashi script the first letter is shaped like a chet but is the Rashi alef, followed by final mem. The second word is שבת. Primary was right; the independent reading's (בשבת) is rejected.

s24 band0/1: no yod. Qamatz under the lamed and a hiriq dot under the final mem, then the two-dot sof pasuq. Primary's unpointed ending יְרוּשָׁלָם is rejected because the dot under the mem is visible.

decisions.reference: s24 Hashkivenu two אָתָּה vs chatimah
decisions.accepted: וּמַצִּילֵנוּ אָתָּה … וְרַחוּם אָתָּה (qamatz); בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה (patah)
decisions.evidence: s24 band0 line 6: both alefs carry a qamatz (T-shaped) mark. In the seal (band0 last line, band1 line 2) the mark is a plain bar, so patah. All three readings agree.
s24 band3 line 5: מן with final nun, then maqaf, כל, maqaf, ברכתא. Primary's מִכָּל־ is rejected.
s24 band3 line 4: five letters ד ק ד ש א with no vav after the qof. Primary's דְּקוּדְשָׁא is rejected.

s24 band3 line 3: the word is noticeably short and I see the letters ו י ת ר מ ם with no vav between resh and mem. Both earlier readings have the vav (one only tentatively). Moderate confidence, so also listed under pending_human.
s24 band3 last line: a comma is clearly printed after בעלמא. Primary dropped it.
s24 band1 Veshamru line 2: the middle letter is short like a yod, not a full-height vav. Agrees with primary; the independent reading's הִוא is rejected.
s24 band1: four letters ל ע ל ם with no vav, so defective. Primary's לְעוֹלָם is rejected.
s24 band1 line 3: the Tetragrammaton is printed in full here, while Hashkivenu, Zekhor and the chatimah use יְיָ. Kept as printed.
s24 band2: a small label before יתגדל. It looks like three letters, fully spelled, but the glyphs are tiny.
s25 band1 line 4: the mark after 'ever' is a comma. Primary's semicolon is rejected.
s25 band2: nothing is printed after 'Lord' at the line end.

decisions.accepted: colon for the two-dot sof pasuq; period where a single dot is printed
decisions.evidence: Single dots appear after עוֹלָם and שְׁלוֹמֶךָ in Hashkivenu, after אָמֵן in Kaddish paragraph 5, and after עָלְמַיָּא. Two dots appear at the ends of verses and at the end of the Kaddish.

pending_human: s24 Tik'u בַּכֶּסֶה vs בַּכֵּסֶה: the vowel under the kaf is hard to read. It looks most like a segol, but I can't rule out a tsere. I recorded segol; the primary reading had tsere.
s24 Kaddish וְיִתְרֹמַם vs וְיִתְרוֹמַם: I read no vav. Please confirm on the original.
s24 speaker label חזן: please confirm the letters, which may be a ligature.
s24 (אם שבת): I see no pointing in the Rashi script, but a faint speck near the first letter can't be excluded.
